title: A lecture on memory
sentences: Memory is not a recording but a reconstruction; each time we recall an event, we rebuild it, and in doing so may subtly alter it.
This explains why eyewitness testimony, though delivered with great confidence, can be unreliable.
Confidence, in other words, is a poor guide to accuracy.

title: A debate on translation
sentences: It is often said that translation is betrayal, yet that view presupposes that meaning resides entirely in the words.

The real failure is not liberty but indifference to the reader.
